The test image shows a corn ear with damaged kernels at the tip — brown/tan discolored kernels with white/grayish mold material. This is a **seed/pod** part. Candidates: Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Common_Smut, Head_Smut, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.

Now viewing one reference per class, starting with the most likely candidates.

Now I have my 16 views across 16 different classes. Let me analyze.

**Test image analysis:**
- Corn ear with damage concentrated at the **tip**
- Brown/tan discolored, somewhat shrunken kernels at tip
- White/grayish mold material visible between kernels
- No obvious olive-green powder (rules out Aspergillus)
- No clear pink/red color (less likely Gibberella)
- Damage at tip, not base (less likely Diplodia which starts at base)

**Comparison to references:**
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Whitish to pink mold at ear tip — the tip location and whitish material match well
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Heavy olive-green powder — NOT like test image
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Clear pink/red mold at tip — test image lacks that color
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: White mycelium from BASE — test is tip damage
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Green-gray mold on husk exterior — NOT like test
- **Common_Smut / Head_Smut**: Galls/dark spore masses — clearly different

The test image best matches **Fusarium_Disease**: whitish material at the tip with brown/discolored kernels, consistent with Fusarium ear rot starting at the tip after insect entry.
